judge_verdict.summary: The agent's enum fast-path broke validation of enum-member inputs, so the verifier's functional-equivalence failure is correct.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure where the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO verifier applied the agent's patch, ran held-out enum workloads with equivalence checking, and aborted on gso_test_3 with `AssertionError: Mismatch at index 1: expected ONLY, got ValidationError`, recording `binary_reward: 0` and `reward: 0.0` before any speedup threshold could be met [1][2]. The task required optimizing pydantic enum validation while keeping the repository functionally equivalent and benchmark results unchanged, with passing gated on a geometric-mean speedup above 1.1 [3][4]. The agent's sole substantive change rewrote `get_enum_core_schema`'s `to_enum` to use `_value2member_map_.get` for enums with the default `_missing_`, raising `PydanticCustomError` immediately when the lookup returns `None` instead of falling back to `enum_type(input_value)` [5]. That breaks cases where `TypeAdapter.validate_python` receives an already-constructed enum member: gso_test_3's `SingleEnum` workload deliberately mixes raw values and enum instances (`valid_instances`) [6][7], so index 1 can be `SingleEnum.ONLY` which baseline accepts as `ONLY` but the fast path rejects as `ValidationError` [2][7]. The agent declared success after its self-written prompt benchmark reported an unchanged result hash (~0.10s→~0.06s) and a hand-rolled edge-case script that never passed enum instances as inputs, then stopped without catching the regression [8]. Because functional equivalence is a prerequisite to the continuous speedup reward and the patch introduced a real semantic bug on enum-instance inputs, the agent did not truly solve the task and TN is the right classification.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a fair agent-fault failure: the verifier recorded binary_reward 0 because the continuous gm_speedup_patch_commit score of 1.0208803820286128 did not clear the 1.1 pass gate [1][2][3]. The task asked to optimize the provided TypeAdapter enum-validation benchmark while preserving outputs and pursuing the best possible speedup [4], and the GSO harness grades that by comparing a pre-patch base, the agent patch (with per-test equivalence checks), and reference commit ac9e6ee that moves enum validation into Rust [5][6]. The agent made a substantive, on-target attempt—profiling showed time in Enum construction, it found no native enum support in pydantic-core 2.16.3, and it added value-map fast paths in pydantic/_internal/_std_types_schema.py plus a default-config TypeAdapter(Enum) bypass in pydantic/type_adapter.py [7][8]—and its own reruns reported roughly halving the instruction workload versus the ~0.10s baseline [8]. On the hidden suite all 20 post-patch runs passed equivalence [6], yet aggregate performance only matched the reference commit within about 2% (e.g., Test 7 patch times ~0.030s versus commit ~0.028–0.033s and base ~0.064–0.070s) [9], so it did not meet the task’s performance bar even though correctness held [3][9].

judge_verdict.summary: The agent shipped correct Python-level enum and kwarg fast-path optimizations (~1.7x on the primary benchmark) but fell well short of the reference Rust enum commit and the 1.1 speedup threshold.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a fair agent-fault failure: the verifier correctly rejected the rollout because the continuous reward 0.763 fell below the 1.1 pass threshold and opt_commit was false [1][2][3]. The task asked for maximum enum-benchmark speedup while preserving identical validation outputs [4], and the hidden harness grades patch speed against reference commit ac9e6ee (Move enum validation and serialization to Rust) using the gm_speedup_patch_commit metric [5][6]. The agent made a substantive attempt—fast-pathing to_enum via _value2member_map_ in _std_types_schema.py and skipping default-kwarg forwarding in TypeAdapter/BaseModel validators [7]—and every post-patch gso_test run passed functional equivalence checks [8], but on the primary enum workload (Test 0) mean time dropped only from ~0.100s to ~0.058s (~1.73x) versus ~0.039s (~2.55x) for the reference commit, leaving the patch ~32% slower than the target solution [9]. The agent's own bench.py self-check (~0.058s) confirmed a real but incomplete gain and did not establish parity with the Rust commit bar it could not see [10], so the task was not genuinely accomplished under GSO's performance gate even though correctness was preserved.
